question: What can exhaustive loss-landscape and learning-trajectory analysis of a minimal sigmoid XOR network reveal about convergence, parameter drift, minibatch effects, and statistical-mechanical phase analogies?

key_findings.claim: Training the two-hidden-neuron XOR network exhibits a plateau, a sudden entry into an attraction basin, and a slow power-law loss tail even while parameter magnitudes continue drifting.
key_findings.evidence: Across learning rates and hidden widths, loss initially sits near 0.25 from small sigmoid parameters, then drops, and later follows an approximate tau^-gamma decay; gamma is about one for the minimal two-hidden-neuron network. Activation traces show the two hidden units separating to encode the XOR cases.

key_findings.claim: Two-dimensional slices through the nine-parameter loss surface contain plateaus, channels, trenches, and multiple basins that explain why gradient descent can converge while weights have no unique finite optimum.
key_findings.evidence: All 36 parameter-pair slices differ, but repeated motif classes appear around several zero-loss solutions. Embedded backpropagation paths follow shallow gradients into channels; randomized single-case batches fragment the surface, while averaging 100 randomized surfaces recovers smoother full-batch structure.

anchors.section: C Analysis of the Loss Landscape

key_findings.claim: A density-of-loss construction yields microcanonical-entropy curves whose convex intruders shrink as hidden width increases, suggesting finite-size barriers disappear with overparameterization.
key_findings.evidence: The paper estimates S(L)=log g(L) over parameter space and interprets convex regions as transition barriers in an annealing analogy. Curves for 2, 6, 10, 14, and 18 hidden neurons become progressively smoother, but this is an analogy on XOR rather than evidence of thermodynamic phase transitions in large networks.

anchors.section: D Density of Loss and Microcanonical Entropy

method.core_idea: Exploit a nine-parameter XOR network small enough for dense trajectory, slice, and parameter-space density measurements.
method.mechanism: The authors train sigmoid networks with backpropagation and alternative batching, enumerate zero-loss parameter sets, scan all parameter-pair cross-sections around solutions, trace gradients through those surfaces, and estimate a microcanonical density of loss for several hidden widths.
assumptions: Mechanisms visible in minimal XOR remain conceptually informative for larger networks.
Two-dimensional slices preserve relevant features of the nine-dimensional landscape.
Loss can play the role of energy and log parameter-volume at fixed loss can play the role of entropy.

techniques.role: Makes parameter and activation trajectories directly inspectable rather than projecting a large model.
Maps local channels, plateaus, and basins around multiple XOR solutions.
Quantifies parameter-space volume at fixed loss and its change with hidden width.

evaluations.setting: Sigmoid XOR networks with 2 to 18 hidden neurons
evaluations.metric: loss trajectories, convergence epochs, parameter/activation paths, and microcanonical entropy
evaluations.result: The minimal network shows plateau-drop-power-law convergence and entropy barriers; increased width smooths the entropy curve and accelerates convergence.
evaluations.baseline: Different learning rates, full versus randomized batches, and wider hidden layers.

limitations: The task has four examples and the smallest nontrivial architecture, so external validity to deep networks is untested.
Two-dimensional slices can omit saddle connections and barriers in the remaining seven dimensions.
The microcanonical analogy lacks a thermodynamic limit, order-parameter validation, or behavioral prediction beyond this toy system.
Reviewer inference: persistent sigmoid parameter drift partly reflects saturation and nonidentifiability rather than a general learning phase.
failure_modes: Changing activation, loss, regularization, or optimizer removes the reported landscape motifs.
Random slice choices produce a misleading picture of high-dimensional connectivity.
Entropy estimates depend strongly on the bounded parameter region and sampling resolution.
reusable_insights: Minimal networks can expose exact symmetry and nonidentifiability that are difficult to separate at scale.
Report both loss convergence and parameter convergence because saturating models can achieve one without the other.
Statistical-mechanics analogies become useful only when paired with measurable finite-size predictions.
open_questions: Which findings survive ReLU, cross-entropy, weight decay, momentum, and adaptive optimization?
Can microcanonical loss entropy prospectively predict convergence time or generalization on larger tasks?
How do full high-dimensional basin connections compare with the reported two-coordinate slices?

competitive_landscape.title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. develop filter-normalized projections to compare high-dimensional deep-network landscapes and generalization. This paper instead exhaustively scans every parameter pair in a tiny network and follows exact activation/parameter trajectories, sacrificing scale for local completeness.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep learning versus kernel learning: an empirical study of loss landscape geometry and the time evolution of the Neural Tangent Kernel
competitive_landscape.difference: Fort et al. diagnose an early chaotic transition with geometry and NTK measurements across realistic deep networks. The XOR study resolves individual parameters and adds loss-density entropy, but does not test whether its phase analogy explains those large-scale regimes.

competitive_landscape.title: Dissecting the Effects of SGD Noise in Distinct Regimes of Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: That work isolates how SGD noise affects realistic networks across training regimes. The XOR study compares randomized and full batches geometrically but uses a four-case toy setting and emphasizes deterministic landscape topology and finite-size entropy barriers.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after comparison: the distinctive element is the microcanonical density-of-loss analysis combined with unusually exhaustive parameter-level XOR trajectories. The study is best treated as a mechanistic toy model and hypothesis generator, not evidence that large-network learning literally undergoes the same phase transitions.
reviewer_notes: All trajectory figures, 36-slice discussion, randomized-batch comparison, entropy construction, width study, and references were reviewed. Primary competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
